title: Titagarh Rail Systems Ltd - 532966 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Titagarh invoiced 51 metro cars in Q1 FY27 (up from 30), with order book at about INR28,600-28,700 crore including JV share.
summary.overview: Management described the quarter as broadly on expected lines, with metro car invoicing rising to 51 from 30 in the prior quarter and the passenger rail system (PRS) reaching its highest quarterly revenue, now about 30%+ of total revenue. Receipt of option-quantity wagon orders from Indian Railways addressed near-term wagon demand uncertainty, and the Vande Bharat JV agreement with BHEL was finally signed. Management reiterated FY28 targets of about 275 metro cars and 192 Vande Bharat coaches, and a return to 1,000 wagons per month by Q4 FY27, while saying Vande Bharat prototype timelines have been re-scheduled. Several answers on project-level detail, traction motor volumes and capex were deflected as competitively sensitive.

segments.name: Passenger Rail System (PRS) - Metro
segments.commentary: 51 metro cars invoiced in the quarter; management aims to get close to the 200-car annual run rate and projects about 275 cars in FY28 across Mumbai and other projects. Bangalore expected to complete this year; Surat and Ahmedabad have a couple of trains delivered each.

segments.name: PRS - Mainline / Vande Bharat
segments.commentary: Contract for 1,280 cars plus 30% option; first prototype expected for testing by Q4 FY27, with the contract implying a second train around 2-3 months later and about 3 months of testing before series clearance. Pune aluminium coach (12 trains option) first Indian-made aluminium coach targeted Q1-Q2 FY28, delivery Q3-Q4 FY28.

segments.name: Freight Rail System (FRS) - Wagons
segments.commentary: Option-quantity wagon orders received from Indian Railways; management targets returning to 1,000 wagons per month by Q4 FY27. Visibility stated at three to four quarters.

segments.name: Propulsion and Components
segments.commentary: Vande Bharat propulsion to be supplied by BHEL under the consortium; in-house propulsion planned after ramp-up per roadmap. Traction motor volumes in Q1 not disclosed; management to check whether the number can be published.

guidance_outlook: Metro: aim for close to 200 cars in FY27; about 275 cars projected for FY28 including Mumbai and other projects.
Vande Bharat: 192 coaches projected by FY28, contingent on prototype testing per contract schedule.
Wagons: return to 1,000 wagons per month by Q4 FY27.
Existing order book expected to be executed by FY28 end; management says new metro gestation period should be shorter due to platforms created by current contracts.
Pune aluminium metro: first India-made aluminium coach Q1-Q2 FY28; first train delivery Q3-Q4 FY28.
Capex: management says the propulsion project is within the previously announced capex plan, with no enhancement needed.
capex_capacity: Vande Bharat mainline facility is separate from the metro line at Uttarpara and is ready to reach target production once the first prototype is tested.
Vande Bharat prototype in full production: car bodies mostly done, furnishing ongoing.
Mumbai Line 6 prototype expected Q4 FY27 (or Q1 CY2027), with Line 5 prototype immediately after; car body production has begun.
Pune aluminium: production bay under construction; flat-pack equipment largely acquired to replace imports from Italy (associate Firema).
Propulsion: management says most capex is already invested and no increase in capex is needed for in-house propulsion.
demand_pricing: Metro tenders in pipeline across Bhubaneswar, Pune, Delhi, Chennai, Nagpur, Ahmedabad, Surat, Patna and others; management declined to size the company's win share.
Wagon demand: plan to reach 40% market share and billion-tonne freight target unchanged; railway traffic rose sharply in last 2-3 months.
Vande Bharat: management sees no need for near-term new tenders given the 1,280-car contract plus option; delivery continues for 4-5 years.
Management says delays are usually absorbed with price-variation and rescheduling, with no penalties; the company is described as the only Indian private player established in metro rolling stock.
Siemens MoU is non-binding and non-exclusive, for metro rolling stock (not wagons), targeting global projects with Indian cost-effective manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Are there delays in metro coaches and Vande Bharat projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Vande Bharat timelines were re-scheduled after changes from 16 to 24 coaches and specification changes. Projects are largely on time, and customers typically accept rescheduling without penalties.

qa_highlights.question: How confident are you of 192 Vande Bharat coaches by FY28 given metro ramp-up history?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the contract schedule: prototype, second train within 2-3 months, about 3 months of testing, then series clearance. It declined to compare metro and Vande Bharat execution in detail and invited analysts to visit the plant.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Mumbai Lines 5 and 6 delayed, and what is the FY28 volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays came from design freeze with the customer and supply-chain issues, including electronic chips after the Gulf War. The Government allowed rescheduling. Line 6 prototype is expected Q4 FY27; management projects about 275 cars in FY28 company-wide, with no project-level split.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Bangalore, Gujarat and Pune metros?
qa_highlights.answer: Bangalore is likely to complete this year; Surat and Ahmedabad have a couple of trains each delivered. Pune's option is 12 aluminium trains, with first India-made aluminium coach in Q1-Q2 FY28 and first delivery in Q3-Q4 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline and supply-chain status, and are wheelset issues behind?
qa_highlights.answer: Wagon visibility is three to four quarters, with the 40% market share plan unchanged. Metro pipeline is in tenders. Management said wheelset challenges are behind for now and the Ramkrishna Forgings JV will add capacity. Execution time for new projects can be as short as 12 months for high carry-over projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vande Bharat prototype delay hit margins, and will wagon production increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the delay affects cash flow and overheads but not margins, since direct costs are price-variation linked. Wagon production will be ramped back to 1,000 per month by Q4 FY27. The Siemens MoU covers metro coaches, not wagons.

risks_watch: Vande Bharat prototype timing (Q4 FY27) and the contract's test-and-clearance schedule; delays may hit cash flow and overheads.
Electronic component and Gulf-war-related supply chain constraints affecting metro and Vande Bharat delivery schedules.
Wagon demand is lumpy and depends on Indian Railways orders; the option-quantity visibility covers about three to four quarters.
Order book is expected to be exhausted by FY28 end, so new metro and wagon orders are needed.
Pune aluminium coach production start and first delivery depend on the new bay being completed in Q1-Q2 FY28.
Management did not disclose traction motor volumes or project-level metro details, limiting visibility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and the metro and wagon ramp-up, but cautious on timelines, with repeated caveats that engineered products can slip a quarter. Evasive on project-level detail, traction motor numbers, the win share in new metro tenders and the high-speed strategy, citing competitive sensitivity.
key_quotes: The most important of that being the number of metro cars invoiced during the quarter, which has gone up to 51, which means that we have been able to hit the run rate of 200 cars that was targeted for the year.
The short answer to your question for Vande Bharat is that it is not going to impact the margin.

We do not believe that we will be impacted beyond the period that the Government of India circular permits us, and we will be on track to deliver the prototype train for Line 6 in Q4 of this financial year.

growth.why: Management targets close to 200 metro cars in FY27 and 275 in FY28, 192 Vande Bharat coaches by FY28 and wagons back to 1,000/month by Q4 FY27, backed by an INR28,600-28,700 crore order book and 51 metro cars invoiced, though Vande Bharat prototype timing has slipped and no revenue growth % or capacity utilisation was stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says the Vande Bharat delay hits cash flow and overheads but not margins, since direct costs are price-variation linked, so no margin expansion was guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Mumbai Line 6 prototype expected Q4 FY27, Vande Bharat Uttarpara mainline facility ready once prototype is tested, and Pune aluminium bay under construction for Q1-Q2 FY28; metro target 275 cars in FY28 versus 51 invoiced in Q1 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets close to 200 metro cars in FY27 and about 275 in FY28, 192 Vande Bharat coaches by FY28, and wagons back to 1,000 per month by Q4 FY27, against 51 metro cars invoiced in Q1 FY27 (up from 30).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says the propulsion project sits within the previously announced capex plan with no enhancement needed, and most capex is already invested; no utilisation level was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held (metro close to 200 in FY27, wagons to 1,000/month by Q4 FY27) and Vande Bharat prototype timelines were re-scheduled, leaving no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Vande Bharat prototype was rescheduled from the original plan after the 16-to-24 coach change, Q4 FY27 prototype depends on testing, and Mumbai Lines 5/6 slipped on design freeze and electronic chip supply issues.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First India-made aluminium coach for Pune targeted Q1-Q2 FY28 with first train delivery Q3-Q4 FY28, under the 12-train option.

rows.label: Order book to be executed by FY28 end; new metro and wagon orders needed
rows.why: Order book of INR28,600-28,700 crore incl. JV share is expected to be exhausted by FY28 end, and metro tenders across about 8 cities are in the pipeline with no win share disclosed.

rows.label: Siemens MoU for global metro rolling stock
rows.why: The MoU is non-binding and non-exclusive, covering metro rolling stock only (not wagons), so it is a possible but unquantified pipeline source.

rows.label: Price-variation recovery on delays
rows.why: Management says delays are absorbed through price-variation and rescheduling with no penalties, which protects margins even as cash flow and overheads are hit by the Vande Bharat delay.

tone.note: Management was confident on the metro and wagon ramp-up and the 275-car FY28 target, but cautious on Vande Bharat prototype timing and evasive on project-level detail, traction motor volumes and win share; analysts pushed on metro execution history and the 192-coach FY28 target.
